ENGLISH: The Road to Jericho
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶利哥路上

ENGLISH: The Good Samaritan
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 好撒玛利亚人

ENGLISH: A lawyer asks Jesus a question. Jesus answers with a story — and you wake up inside it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个人被强盗打个半死，躺在路边。三个人走过，只有一个停下来。

ENGLISH: c. AD 30, on the road from Jerusalem down to Jericho — seventeen miles of limestone cliffs, sharp bends, and no soldiers.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元 30 年，从耶路撒冷下耶利哥的那条路——十七英里的石灰岩山道，弯多，没有兵丁巡守。

ENGLISH: A lawyer has just tested a teacher named Jesus with a question: “Who is my neighbour?” Jesus answers with a story, and you find yourself standing inside it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一位律法师刚刚用问题试探耶稣：「谁是我的邻舍？」耶稣没有正面回答，而是讲了一个故事，而你此刻就站在故事里面。

ENGLISH: A traveller lies beaten in the ditch. A priest and a temple assistant have already seen him and crossed the road. Someone still has to stop — and in this story the one who stops is the man nobody expects.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个旅人被打个半死，躺在沟边。祭司和圣殿的助手已经先后从另一边走了过去。总得有人停下来——而在这个故事里，停下来的正是最出人意料的那个人。

ENGLISH: A lawyer asks “who is my neighbour?” wanting to limit the obligation. Jesus tells a parable in which the religious professionals pass by and a despised Samaritan stops — then turns the question around: which of the three was a neighbour?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 律法师问「谁是我的邻舍」，其实是想给责任划一条边界。耶稣没跟他辩，只讲了一个故事：该懂的人绕道走了，被看不起的撒玛利亚人却停下——然后反问：这三个人里，谁是那落在强盗手中之人的邻舍？

ENGLISH: Mercy is a verb with a price tag.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 怜悯不只是一个感觉而已，是要付上代价的。

ENGLISH: The Samaritan’s compassion cost him oil, wine, money, time, reputation, and his own donkey. Love that costs nothing is usually just a feeling.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 撒玛利亚人为这份怜悯付上了代价：油、酒、银子、时间、名声，还有他自己那头驴。不肯付代价的爱，多半只是一时心软。

ENGLISH: Who is the neighbour you find it hardest to love — and what would one small act look like?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 谁是你现在最难去爱的邻舍？一个很小的动作，可以是什么？

ENGLISH: Someone whose views I cannot stand
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个我完全没法认同的人

ENGLISH: The Samaritan and the Jew disagreed about almost everything sacred. The bandage came first. Luke 10:33–34
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 撒玛利亚人和犹太人在几乎每件神圣的事上都不对付。可他还是先缠上了绷带。路加福音 10:33–34

ENGLISH: Someone I can help, but it will genuinely cost me
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个我帮得了、但真的要付出代价的人

ENGLISH: Two denarii was real money. Count the cost honestly — then give anyway. Luke 10:35
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 二两银子是实打实的工钱，差不多是两天的收入。先老实算算要付多少，然后还是照样给出去。路加福音 10:35

ENGLISH: Someone I have walked past without really seeing
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个我天天经过、却从没真正看见的人

ENGLISH: The priest “saw him” and passed by. Seeing is not the same as noticing. Luke 10:31
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 祭司「看见他」，就从那边过去了。看见了，不等于放在心上。路加福音 10:31

ENGLISH: You are sitting in the dust outside a village, listening to a teacher. A lawyer stands to test Him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你坐在村外的尘土里，听一位老师讲道。一名律法师站起来试探他。

SPEAKER: lawyer
ENGLISH: Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? … And who is my neighbour?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「夫子，我该做什么才可以承受永生？……谁是我的邻舍呢？」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He is not asking for information. He is asking where the boundary is — who he is allowed to leave out.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他不是来求答案的。他想问的是：这条线划在哪儿，谁可以被划在外面。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves…
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「有一个人从耶路撒冷下耶利哥去，落在强盗手中……」

ENGLISH: The road rises up around you: seventeen miles of switchbacks, limestone, and shadowed places perfect for an ambush. You are in the story now.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 四周的路忽然立了起来：十七英里的急弯、石灰岩、正适合埋伏的阴影。你已经站在故事里了。

ENGLISH: Walk fast, before the sun gets high
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 趁着日头还低，快点走

ENGLISH: You make good time. That is the trouble with hurrying — you arrive at the bad part sooner.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你走得很快。麻烦也在这儿——你更早到了那段险路。

ENGLISH: Walk with a companion and keep your eyes open
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 结伴走，留意四周

ENGLISH: You notice the fresh blood before you notice the man. Your companion grips your arm.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你先看见新鲜的血迹，才看见那个人。同伴抓紧了你的手臂。

ENGLISH: Pray for safety on the road before you set out
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 出发前先为路上的平安祷告

ENGLISH: You ask God to make you useful, not just safe. It is a dangerous prayer, though you do not know it yet.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你求神让你成为一个有用的人，而不只是个安全的人。这祷告很危险，当时你还不知道。

ENGLISH: Halfway down, in a bend of the road where the rock walls close in, a man is lying in the dust.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 走到半路，一处岩壁收紧的弯道里，有人躺在尘土中。

ENGLISH: The thieves have stripped him, beaten him, and left him half dead. His breathing is shallow. There is no one else in sight.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 强盗剥去了他的衣裳，把他打个半死。他的呼吸很浅，四下里没有别人。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: This is where the parable gets uncomfortable. Everyone who comes down this road has to decide something.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 故事讲到这里，就不那么好听了。每一个从这条路走过的人，都得做个决定。

ENGLISH: Cross to the far side — it could be a trap
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 绕到另一边去——说不定是圈套

ENGLISH: You give him a wide berth. Your heart is still hammering when you reach the next bend. Being safe and being right are not the same thing.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你绕得很远。走到下一个弯时，心还在乱跳。安全是一回事，做对是另一回事，这两件事并不总在一起。

ENGLISH: Kneel and check if he is still breathing
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪下探一探他还有没有气

ENGLISH: He is alive. Barely. You tear a strip from your own cloak and press it against the worst wound. There is not much else you can do.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他还活着，勉强活着。你从自己的斗篷上撕下一条布，按住最深的伤口。你能做的也只有这些。

ENGLISH: Shout for help from the ridge above
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 朝山脊上喊人

ENGLISH: Your voice echoes off the limestone. Nobody answers — but two figures appear at the top of the road.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 喊声在石灰岩之间撞来撞去。没有人回应——但那人的手指动了一下。他听见了。

ENGLISH: You are kneeling in the dust with blood on your hands when you hear sandals on the stone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你在他身边蹲下来。他需要的不只是同情，还要油、酒、绷带，和一头能驮他的牲口。

ENGLISH: A priest comes down the road. He sees the man — clearly sees him — and passes by on the other side.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 远处有脚步声。一个祭司从坡上下来，正往圣殿的方向去。

ENGLISH: Later, a Levite does exactly the same.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他看见了他。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Do not be too quick to despise them. They may have been afraid, or late, or certain that touching a corpse would make them unclean. Good reasons are always available.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 然后他从另一边走了过去。接着是一名利未人，也一样绕开了。

ENGLISH: Shout after them to come back
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 追上去问那两个人为什么

ENGLISH: They do not turn around. Your voice cracks on the last word. The man at your feet does not notice.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们都有理由：礼仪上的洁净、律法的规定、怕惹麻烦。理由从来不缺。而那个人还躺在尘土里。

ENGLISH: Stay with the wounded man and keep pressure on the wound
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 留下来，尽力先把伤口包好

ENGLISH: You stay. It is unglamorous and it takes a long time. Most mercy looks exactly like this.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你的手在抖，还是把布条系紧了。柯林在旁边轻声说：「记住这一刻，你正在做一件神圣的事。」

ENGLISH: Ask Corin why the holy men walked away
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 走到路中间，拦下下一个路人

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: “Because knowing the Law and loving your neighbour are not the same achievement,” he says quietly. “I have been both men.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你拦下一个过路的人。他看看地上的人，又看看自己的行程，摇摇头走了。

ENGLISH: On the road, a priest comes down, sees the body, and crosses to the far side. A Levite follows, does the same, and is gone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 第三个人骑着驴过来。他不是祭司，也不是利未人，是撒玛利亚人——本地的犹太人宁可绕路也不跟他说话的那种人。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: They had Scripture memorised. They were on their way to the temple. And the man in the ditch was still in the ditch.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他看见那人，就动了慈心。

ENGLISH: Then a third traveller appears, leading a donkey — and from his dress, he is a Samaritan. The wounded man is a Jew. The two peoples have hated each other for centuries.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他下驴，把油和酒倒在他的伤处，包扎好，扶他骑上自己的牲口，送到客店里去。

ENGLISH: He stops. He kneels. He pours oil and wine on the wounds.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路上的每一个决定，其实都只用了短短几秒。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Watch closely. This is the part of the story people remember.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林轻声提醒：注意，耶稣没说这个人是「好人」，只说他「动了慈心」。

ENGLISH: Go down and offer to carry his supplies
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 帮他一起把伤者抬上驴背

SPEAKER: samaritan
ENGLISH: He looks up, surprised, then nods as if this is the most natural thing in the world. “Hold the oil,” he says. “I will lift him.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你们一起把人抬上去。他沉，路远。撒玛利亚人一路牵着驴走。

ENGLISH: Ask him why he is helping an enemy
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问他为什么肯为一个陌生人停下

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He does not answer. He simply keeps bandaging. Corin says: “The parable never tells us his reasons. I think that is deliberate — mercy that needs a reason can be argued away.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他想了一会儿：「因为要是躺在那儿的是我，我也盼着有人肯停一下。」

ENGLISH: Take the donkey’s lead rope and follow
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 先跑去客店把房间打点好

ENGLISH: The donkey is calm. The man on its back is not. You lead them both down the long road toward an inn.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你先跑到客店。店主起初不太情愿——直到看见那枚银币。

ENGLISH: The Samaritan finishes the bandage and lifts the man onto his own donkey, standing him up carefully as if he were something fragile.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你要尽心、尽性、尽力、尽意爱主你的神；又要爱邻舍如同自己。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He has somewhere to be too. His journey is now slower, his beast is carrying a stranger, and his oil is nearly gone. Compassion always spends something.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 律法师想证明自己问得有理，又追问：「谁是我的邻舍呢？」

SPEAKER: samaritan
ENGLISH: Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶稣把问题翻了个面：这三个人里，哪一个才是那落在强盗手中之人的邻舍？

ENGLISH: At the inn the Samaritan sets two denarii on the counter — about two days’ wages — and makes the innkeeper promise to look after the man.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 客店里，撒玛利亚人拿出二两银子——差不多是两天的工钱。

SPEAKER: innkeeper
ENGLISH: Two days’ wages? For a stranger?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你且照应他，此外所费用的，我回来必还你。」

SPEAKER: samaritan
ENGLISH: When I come again, I will repay thee whatsoever thou spendest more.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这不是一时的感动，而是一份要继续下去的承诺。他还会回来。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He does not just feel pity. He commits money, time, and his own return journey. That is what makes it love instead of a sentiment.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林说：怜悯很少是一时的心情，多半是一个决定，还要算上一笔代价。

ENGLISH: Offer to sit with the man through the night
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 替他把欠店主的账一笔笔记清楚

ENGLISH: You take the stool by the bed. Somewhere around midnight he opens his eyes. You are the first person he sees.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你一笔一笔记清楚。有些爱，就落在一张写得明明白白的账上。

ENGLISH: Tell everyone in the inn what happened on the road
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 留下来守伤者一夜

ENGLISH: By evening half the courtyard knows the story. The priest will not be pleased. The wounded man will not be alone again.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 夜里他发起烧来。你用湿布替他擦额头，直到天快亮时他终于睡稳了。

ENGLISH: Ask the innkeeper to keep the coins safe until he returns
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问撒玛利亚人打算什么时候回来

SPEAKER: innkeeper
ENGLISH: The innkeeper wraps them carefully. “He said he would come back,” he mutters. “Most people do not.” He is still holding the coins when you leave.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我不知道，」他说，「但我会回来。」你知道他说的是真的。

ENGLISH: The road, the inn, the dust — all of it folds back into the scroll. You are sitting in the village again.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路、客店、尘土，全都折回书卷里。你又坐回了村外。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你想，这三个人哪一个是落在强盗手中的邻舍呢？」

SPEAKER: lawyer
ENGLISH: He that shewed mercy on him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「是怜悯他的。」

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Go, and do thou likewise.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你去照样行吧。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He never actually answers “who is my neighbour?” He replaces it with a better question: whose neighbour will you be?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「谁是我的邻舍」这个问题，他其实一直没有回答。他换了一个更好的问题：你愿意成为谁的邻舍？

ENGLISH: Answer with the lawyer: the one who showed mercy
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把这句话记在自己的书卷上

ENGLISH: Jesus nods. You have understood the parable — which is the easy half.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你把这句话写下来。后来你会一次又一次翻回这一页。

ENGLISH: Answer: the priest, because he knew the Law
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问耶稣：如果我做不到呢

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Corin winces. Jesus gently repeats the story, more slowly this time. Being corrected by kindness is its own kind of mercy.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他看着你，语气里没有责备，只有邀请：「所以你缺的不是意志力，是身边那个具体的人。」

ENGLISH: Stay silent and let the question sit with you
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 回头看一眼那个撒玛利亚人

ENGLISH: You say nothing. But you notice that you can still feel the weight of the man on the donkey. That is a beginning.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他已经上路了，驴背上的位置空着——因为那个人还躺在客店里。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The lawyer wanted a boundary. Jesus gave him a mirror.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这个比喻里最危险的，不是强盗，而是那条允许你从旁边绕过去的路。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The neighbour in this story is not a category of person who deserves your help. It is a person you decide to become.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶稣没有叫我们做英雄，他叫我们做邻舍。

ENGLISH: The scroll turns. The smell of the road lingers on your clothes.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷翻页了，可那条耶利哥路还在你脚下。
